Parenteral (or inhaled for CF); not meal-related
Use if clearly needed; generally considered low risk
Reduce dose ~20-25% in prolonged severe hepatic impairment
Renal/hepatic function on prolonged use; signs of colitis
summary: Aztreonam is a monobactam beta-lactam with activity essentially limited to aerobic Gram-negative bacteria, including Pseudomonas aeruginosa. It is given IV/IM (an inhaled form exists for cystic fibrosis P. aeruginosa). Because of its unique monobactam structure it has low cross-reactivity with penicillins/cephalosporins (except ceftazidime, which shares a side chain), making it a useful option in beta-lactam-allergic patients.
indications: Urinary tract infections (complicated and uncomplicated) due to susceptible Gram-negatives
Lower respiratory tract infections including pneumonia and bronchitis
Septicemia due to susceptible Gram-negative organisms
Intra-abdominal infections (with anaerobic/Gram-positive coverage as needed)
Inhaled form: improve respiratory symptoms in cystic fibrosis patients with P. aeruginosa

dosage.d: 500 mg or 1 g IV/IM every 8-12 h
30 mg/kg IV every 6-8 h (severe: every 6 h)
Usual initial dose, then halve maintenance dose
75 mg nebulized three times daily x 28 days
dosage.n: Use a bronchodilator first; separate cycles

admin: Reconstitute and administer IV (bolus over 3-5 min or infusion over 20-60 min) or by deep IM injection
Doses >1 g should be given intravenously
For inhaled form, use the supplied nebulizer and a bronchodilator beforehand
Adjust maintenance dose for renal impairment
Reserve for proven or strongly suspected susceptible Gram-negative infection; add Gram-positive/anaerobic coverage if needed
moa: Aztreonam is a bactericidal monobactam that binds with high affinity to penicillin-binding protein 3 (PBP-3) of aerobic Gram-negative bacteria, inhibiting cell-wall peptidoglycan synthesis and causing filamentation and lysis. It is stable against many beta-lactamases and lacks meaningful activity against Gram-positive or anaerobic organisms.

relative: History of immediate hypersensitivity to other beta-lactams (low cross-reactivity, but caution; note ceftazidime shares a side chain)

preg: Generally considered acceptable when clearly needed; animal data and clinical experience do not indicate significant risk. Use if benefit justifies use.
lact: Compatible; aztreonam is excreted in breast milk in very low concentrations and is poorly absorbed orally by the infant.
renal: Renally eliminated. Give the usual initial dose, then reduce maintenance dose: halve for CrCl 10-30 mL/min and give one-quarter for CrCl <10 mL/min. Supplement after hemodialysis for serious infections.
hepatic: In serious prolonged infection with hepatic impairment (e.g., cirrhosis), consider a ~20-25% dose reduction. No adjustment needed for short courses.

moderate: Nephrotoxic antibiotics (aminoglycosides) - monitor renal function with concurrent use
minor: Cefoxitin, imipenem - in vitro antagonism (avoid combining beta-lactams that induce beta-lactamases)
interactions.diagnostics: May cause transient elevations in transaminases and a positive Coombs test; generally no urine glucose interference.

monitoring: Renal and hepatic function with prolonged therapy
Signs of superinfection or C. difficile diarrhea
counsel: This antibiotic is given by injection (or inhalation for cystic fibrosis)
Report rash, breathing difficulty, or persistent/bloody diarrhea
Finish the full course as directed
If using the inhaled form, use your bronchodilator first and follow the cycle schedule
Tell your provider about beta-lactam allergies
pk: End of infusion (IV); ~1 h after IM
Store dry powder at room temperature; use reconstituted solution promptly per label
pearls: Spectrum essentially limited to aerobic Gram-negative bacteria, including Pseudomonas aeruginosa
Low cross-reactivity with penicillins/cephalosporins - useful in beta-lactam allergy (but caution with ceftazidime, shared side chain)
No Gram-positive or anaerobic coverage - combine when those are needed
Inhaled formulation is for cystic fibrosis patients with chronic P. aeruginosa
Dose must be reduced for renal impairment
missed: As this is a hospital/clinician-administered (or scheduled nebulized) medication, a missed dose should be given as soon as possible per the treating team; do not double the dose to make up.
overdose: No specific antidote. If overdose is suspected, discontinue and provide supportive care. Hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis can remove aztreonam and may be used in severe overdose, particularly with renal impairment.
